newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds tracked other debt markets on Tuesday and ended slightly lower as profit-taking emerged repeatedly on peaks, dealers said.
But dealers added that Bonos are still strong and are focused on December CPI, due Wednesday morning.
Good news on the inflation trend and the peseta's strength could prod the Bank of Spain to cut the official rate at its regular repo on Thursday, some dealers said.
"But even with a lower-than-expected CPI, say 3.1 percent year-on-year, I do not think the Bank of Spain will move so soon," said Jose Ramon Nunez at Benito y Monjardin in Madrid.
On the cash market, the 10-year spread over Bunds ended at 94 bps versus 91 bps, the low hit yesterday, while the spread over the U.S. widened slightly to seven bps from one.
The yield curve flattened somewhat, after having steepened sharply in the last week, dealers said.
The 9.40 percent April '99 ended at 108.63, with a yield at 5.25 pct and a spread to the 10-year benchmark of around 146 basis points. It was 152 bps yesterday, and 120 a week ago.
In the five-year segment, the 10.1 percent February 2001 ended at 115.94, yielding 5.63 percent with a spread over the 10-year yields of 108 bps versus 112 and 96 bps respectively.

"I still believe that the Spanish yield curve is set to steepen even further. It may be later rather than sooner, but the Bank of Spain will end up cutting its official rate one more time," said Jose Ramon Nunez.
The peseta, which has broken the level of 84 versus the mark less than a week ago, has set a new range. It ended today around 83.55/58 from 83.47/48 at yesterday's close.
